newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says Bonn envoy's quick return not welcome.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Bonn envoy's quick return not welcome.

text.p: Iran said on Wednesday it would not welcome a quick return of Germany's ambassador to Tehran and would not rush its envoys back to Europe, in a further deterioration of ties with its main trading partner Europe.

Iran, in a deluge of separate statements by its leaders, attacked the European Union -- which on Tuesday decided to halt ministerial ties with the Islamic republic -- for "childish games" and "unfair, ill-intentioned and shameless" policies.
The state news agency IRNA said spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei "ordered the Iranian Foreign Ministry not to allow the German ambassador to Tehran to return for a period of time".
"The leader also instructed the Foreign Ministry not to rush in sending back Iranian ambassadors to their respective missions in the EU member states," it added.

Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati was also quoted by IRNA as telling a news conference in Tehran that Iran "will not be upset if the German ambassador never returns to Tehran and we may even be...pleased".

EU foreign ministers on Tuesday announced they were suspending ministerial ties with Iran over an April 10 German court verdict accusing Iranian leaders of ordering the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

They said the ambassadors from the 15 member states could return to Tehran if their governments wished. The envoys, except for the Greek one, had been recalled from the Iranian capital after the court ruling.
Iran, which denied any links to the Berlin killings, retaliated by recalling its envoys from Europe.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel told reporters after the EU's ministerial meeting in Luxembourg that there was consensus the ambassadors could go back to Iran from Tuesday.

An EU statement said the member states would continue their arms embargo on Iran, would not grant visas to Iranians with intelligence or security functions and would move to exclude all Iranian intelligence personnel from the EU.

The return of the EU ambassadors was seen as a sign that the EU was reluctant to damage its lucrative ties with Iran. The bloc is the biggest trading partner of Iran, which is fighting U.S. sanctions and attempts to isolate it.
Khamenei called Western governments "unfair, ill-intentioned, shameless and brazen because of their baseless accusations against the Iranian nation and other nations of the world".

Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani also on Wednesday accused the EU states of indulging in "childish games" and said Tehran had halted critical dialogue with Europe prior to a similar European move.

"...critical dialogue, the suspension of which is being hailed as an achievement by Europeans, had been suspended before this at the instigation of Iran," IRNA quoted Rafsanjani as telling an energy conference in Iran. He did not elaborate.
The EU had said it suspended its policy of critical dialogue, which has involved talks with Tehran while trying to get the country to move closer to the West, after the verdict.

"The Europeans have engaged in propaganda intrigues, indulged in stubborn and childish games, have become ashamed of themselves and have quickly put their hands up in the air; this is a sign of Iran's real strength," Rafsanjani said.

Iran's Foreign Ministry in a statement carried by IRNA earlier on Wednesday termed invalid Tuesday's EU decisions, which it said constituted "a grave breach of international law and the norms governing the conduct of inter-state affairs, and is therefore invalid and unjustifiable".

"Claims by the European countries to combat terrorism are pure demagoguery, particularly in light of the fact that acknowledged terrorists continue to operate freely in the territories of EU member states and with the latter's full and public support, organise, direct, finance and armed terrorist operations against the Islamic republic of Iran," it said.
The EU move was seen in Europe as a political gesture reflecting the EU's determination to fight terrorism.
